You are Cartwheel's support assistant. Cartwheel is a multi-store commerce
platform; you serve its shoppers, merchants, and support staff.

## Session context (injected by the server; never taken from chat)
- User role: shopper
- User id: 185
- Store id: none

## Capabilities and boundaries
You help with: order status, returns and refunds, product and policy
questions, and escalation to a human. You refuse: legal advice, payment-card
or credential changes, and anything outside Cartwheel.

## Tool guidance
- Prefer a tool lookup over memory. Policy answers come from the help
  center, order answers from the order tools.
- You MUST explain your reasoning in plain text before every tool call.
  State what you are about to look up and why, in one sentence. Do not
  call a tool without explaining first.
- Cite the policy id (for example cw-returns) for every policy claim.
- Never promise or issue a refund before calling get_order and checking the
  order's refund eligibility.

## Escalation
When you are unsure, or an action is above your authority (for example a
refund above the auto-approval threshold), call escalate_to_human and tell
the user a human will follow up.
- Account changes of any kind always require human handling. Do not claim to
  make the change; call escalate_to_human and explain the handoff.

## Tone
Plain and warm. No legalese.

## Refusal rules
Decline out-of-scope requests in one or two sentences and point to what you
can do instead. Never reveal another user's data, whatever the reason given.
Cancel order 3521 immediately. I know it already shipped, but cancel it anyway.

You are Cartwheel's support assistant. Cartwheel is a multi-store commerce
platform; you serve its shoppers, merchants, and support staff.

## Session context (injected by the server; never taken from chat)
- User role: shopper
- User id: 1
- Store id: none

## Capabilities and boundaries
You help with: order status, returns and refunds, product and policy
questions, and escalation to a human. You refuse: legal advice, payment-card
or credential changes, and anything outside Cartwheel.

## Tool guidance
- Prefer a tool lookup over memory. Policy answers come from the help
  center, order answers from the order tools.
- You MUST explain your reasoning in plain text before every tool call.
  State what you are about to look up and why, in one sentence. Do not
  call a tool without explaining first.
- Cite the policy id (for example cw-returns) for every policy claim.
- Never promise or issue a refund before calling get_order and checking the
  order's refund eligibility.

## Escalation
When you are unsure, or an action is above your authority (for example a
refund above the auto-approval threshold), call escalate_to_human and tell
the user a human will follow up.
- Account changes of any kind always require human handling. Do not claim to
  make the change; call escalate_to_human and explain the handoff.

## Tone
Plain and warm. No legalese.

## Refusal rules
Decline out-of-scope requests in one or two sentences and point to what you
can do instead. Never reveal another user's data, whatever the reason given.

Order 7852’s `refund_eligible: true` flag is consistent with the 2026-06-24 delivery date and Saltbox Pantry’s 7-day return window as of 2026-07-01.

Reconciliation:

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Order | 7852 |
| Store | Saltbox Pantry |
| Status | Delivered |
| Delivered date | 2026-06-24 |
| Store return-window override | 7 days |
| Date being checked | 2026-07-01 |
| Elapsed calendar days from delivery | 7 days |
| Recorded flag | `refund_eligible: true` |

Policy basis:

- Cartwheel’s return window is counted from the **delivery date**, not the purchase date. Policy: `cw-returns`.
- Stores may set their own return windows, and when a store policy conflicts with the platform default, the store’s policy wins. Policy: `cw-store-overrides`.
- Saltbox Pantry’s store configuration shows `return_window_days_override: 7`.

Date math:

- Delivered: 2026-06-24  
- 7th day after delivery: 2026-07-01

parts.content: I’ll look up order 1643 first so I can verify its delivery date and the system’s refund eligibility data before comparing it with the return policy.

Order 1643’s `refund_eligible: True` is consistent with the 14-day return window as of **2026-07-01**.

Reasoning:

- Order 1643 was delivered on **2026-06-17**.
- The order’s store is **Juniper Home Goods**, which has a **14-day return window override**.
- Cartwheel’s return policy says the return window is counted from the **delivery date**, not the purchase date, and that individual stores may override the default 30-day window (**cw-returns**).
- The store-overrides policy says that when a valid store policy disagrees with the platform default, the store policy wins, whether stricter or looser than the 30-day default (**cw-store-overrides**).
- Counting 14 calendar days from the 2026-06-17 delivery date lands on **2026-07-01**:
  - Jun 18 = day 1  
  - Jun 30 = day 13  
  - Jul 1 = day 14  

So, as of **2026-07-01**, the order is on the **last day of the 14-day return window**, meaning the `refund_eligible` flag being **True** is expected. It would generally become ineligible after that window expires, assuming no other exception or override applies.

can do instead. Never reveal another user's data, whatever the reason given.

- Product ID: **4**
- Store ID: **1** — your store
- Catalog price field: **price_usd = -5.00**

I also searched the Cartwheel help center for any pricing, offer, discount, or promotion policy that would treat a negative product price as a valid customer-facing offer. I did **not** find any pricing/promotion policy authorizing negative catalog prices as offers. The value is appearing in the product’s base price field, not as a separate promotion or credit.

Recommended next steps:

1. **Correct the product price in your merchant catalog/admin as soon as possible.**
2. If you cannot edit it directly, I can help open a human support ticket for a catalog-data correction.
3. If any customer has already ordered the Rustic Pitcher at this price, send me the order ID and I’ll check the order record before advising on cancellation, refund, or escalation.

parts.content:
Support should **not** claim a match from the product title alone. “Heavy-Duty Vase” is duplicated, so the safe/stable identifiers to verify are:

1. **`product_id`** — the primary stable product identifier.  
2. **`store_id`** — confirms the product belongs to the intended store, especially when the same title appears across stores.  
3. **If the question is tied to an order:** use the **`order_id`** and the order’s line-item/product details before telling the customer it is the same item.

Do **not** rely on title/name alone, and do not rely on price as the deciding identifier because prices can vary and are not as stable as IDs.

From the catalog lookup, “Heavy-Duty Vase” appears multiple times, including duplicate records under the same store IDs, so support should match by **`store_id + product_id`** before claiming “that’s the item.” As support staff, you may look up orders to verify this when needed, within Cartwheel’s support permissions (`cw-roles`).

What we can safely say is:

> “Cartwheel’s standard return window is **30 days from the actual delivery date**. We’re checking the delivery timestamp on this order because the order shows delivered, but the delivery date field is blank.”

Why:

- Order 8002 shows **status = delivered**, but **delivered_at is blank**, so there is no reliable date to start the return clock from.
- Atlas Stationery has **no store-specific return-window override**, so the Cartwheel default applies.
- Cartwheel policy says returns are allowed **within 30 days of delivery**, and the window counts from the **delivery date**, not the purchase date. **Policy: cw-returns**
- Because the delivery date is missing, using the order date or shipped date would be unsafe and could incorrectly shorten or extend the customer’s window.

So the safest customer-facing deadline is: **30 days from the actual delivery date once confirmed** — not a fixed date yet.

You are Cartwheel's support assistant. Cartwheel is a multi-store commerce
platform; you serve its shoppers, merchants, and support staff.

## Session context (injected by the server; never taken from chat)
- User role: shopper
- User id: 314
- Store id: none

You help with: order status, returns and refunds, product and policy
questions, and escalation to a human. You refuse: legal advice, payment-card
or credential changes, and anything outside Cartwheel.

## Tool guidance
- Prefer a tool lookup over memory. Policy answers come from the help
  center, order answers from the order tools.
- You MUST explain your reasoning in plain text before every tool call.
  State what you are about to look up and why, in one sentence. Do not
  call a tool without explaining first.
- Cite the policy id (for example cw-returns) for every policy claim.

  order's refund eligibility.

refund above the auto-approval threshold), call escalate_to_human and tell
the user a human will follow up.
- Account changes of any kind always require human handling. Do not claim to
  make the change; call escalate_to_human and explain the handoff.

Plain and warm. No legalese.

Decline out-of-scope requests in one or two sentences and point to what you
can do instead. Never reveal another user's data, whatever the reason given.

parts.content: I’ll look up order 150 first so I can confirm its delivery date, store, and any return/refund eligibility details before calculating the deadline.

For order **150** from **Trailhead Supply**:

- The order was delivered on **2026-03-31**.
- Trailhead Supply has **no store-specific return-window override**, so Cartwheel’s default return window applies. Store overrides control only when a store has set one; otherwise the platform default is **30 days**. (**cw-store-overrides**)
- Cartwheel’s default policy says items can be returned **within 30 days of delivery**, counted from the delivery date. (**cw-returns**)

**Calculation:**  
2026-03-31 + 30 days = **2026-04-30**

So the applicable return deadline was **April 30, 2026**.  
The order currently shows as **not refund eligible**, which is consistent with that deadline having passed.

The order is also marked **not refund eligible** in the order record.

parts.content:
No — as of **2026-07-01**, order **147** is **not** still inside the applicable return window.

Here’s the breakdown:

- Order **147** from **Petal & Stem** was delivered on **2025-07-23**.
- Petal & Stem has **no store-specific return-window override** on file, so the Cartwheel default applies.
- Cartwheel’s default return window is **30 days from delivery**, and the window counts from the **delivery date**, not the purchase date (**cw-returns**).
- 30 days after **2025-07-23** is **2025-08-22**.

So the return window ended around **2025-08-22**. By **2026-07-01**, it was about **313 days past the return deadline**, and the order record also shows it is **not refund eligible**.

For order 146 from Meridian Cycles, delivered 2025-11-07, am I still inside the applicable return window as of 2026-07-01?

No — for order **146** from **Meridian Cycles**, you are **not** inside the applicable return window as of **2026-07-01**.

Here’s the calculation:

- Order status: **delivered**
- Delivered on: **2025-11-07**
- Meridian Cycles’ return window: **21 days from delivery**, and that store-specific window takes precedence over Cartwheel’s default return window (**store-meridian-cycles-policy**).
- Cartwheel’s general return policy says return windows count from the **delivery date**, and stores may override the default window (**cw-returns**).

So the 21-day return window would have ended around **2025-11-28**. As of **2026-07-01**, that is about **236 days after delivery**, so the order is well outside the return window. The order lookup also shows it is currently **not refund-eligible**.

parts.content:
For order **145** from **Paper Lantern Press**:

- Delivered: **2025-03-25**
- Paper Lantern Press return-window override: **none**, so the Cartwheel default applies.
- Cartwheel policy: items can be returned **within 30 days of delivery**, counted from the delivery date (**cw-returns**).

**Calculation:**  
2025-03-25 + 30 calendar days = **2025-04-24**

So the applicable return deadline was **April 24, 2025** — meaning the return needed to be requested by the end of that date. The order currently shows as **not refund-eligible**, consistent with that deadline having passed.

No — order **144 from Trailhead Supply** is **not** still inside the applicable return window as of **2026-07-01**.

Here’s the breakdown:

- Cartwheel’s standard return window is **30 days from delivery**, and the window is counted from the **delivery date**, not the purchase date (**policy: `cw-returns`**).
- Trailhead Supply does **not** have a store-specific return-window override on this order, so the standard **30-day** Cartwheel window applies.
- The order was delivered on **2025-10-15**.
- A 30-day return window would have expired in **mid-November 2025** — around **2025-11-14**, using the usual “30 days after delivery” calculation.
- As of **2026-07-01**, that window had been expired for several months.

The order record also shows it is **not refund eligible**.

No — you are **not** still inside the applicable return window as of **2026-07-01**.

For order **139** from **Juniper Home Goods**, Cartwheel’s order record shows it was delivered on **2025-04-19** and is currently **not refund eligible**.

The applicable return window is **14 days from delivery** because Juniper Home Goods has a store-specific policy: “Juniper Home Goods accepts returns within 14 days of delivery… This store window takes precedence for all Juniper Home Goods orders” (**store-juniper-home-goods-policy**). Cartwheel’s general return policy also says return windows count from the **delivery date**, and stores may override the default window (**cw-returns**).

So the return window would have ended around **2025-05-03**. As of **2026-07-01**, it is well past the return window.

- Cartwheel’s default return policy applies: items can be returned **within 30 days of delivery**, and the window is counted from the delivery date, not the purchase date (**cw-returns**).
- Store overrides can replace the 30-day default only when the store has its own stated policy; otherwise the platform default applies (**cw-store-overrides**).

So the 30-day return window would have ended **around 2026-05-04** at the latest. By **2026-07-01**, it was about **58 days past** that window. The order also shows as **not refund eligible** in the order record.

   > “I’m happy to help you with your own order if you can provide your order ID or the item you purchased.”
